content: To return to the WikiDoc scholar program homepage, click the provided link. Why is it necessary to redirect a page? In some cases, a single topic may be known by multiple names or abbreviations. It is often useful to consolidate all these variations into one central page. For instance, the topic ST Elevation Myocardial Infarction is commonly referred to by several terms, such as STEMI, MI, Acute MI, Myocardial Infarction, or AMI. All of these terms are redirected to the main page titled ST Elevation Myocardial Infarction. How can you create a redirect (redirect command)? To redirect one page (Page A) to another page (Page B), which is also referred to as the target page, you need to use a specific redirect command. This command should be entered at the top of the redirecting page using the edit source function. For example, if you want to redirect the page titled MI to the page titled ST Elevation Myocardial Infarction, you would edit the MI page and insert the appropriate redirect command. How do I redirect to a specific subsection of a page instead of the general page? If you want to redirect a page, such as Alcohol septal ablation, to a specific section within a parent page, for example, a subsection titled Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy interventional cardiology, you can achieve this by specifying the name of the parent page followed by the hash symbol () and the name of the subsection. This allows the redirect to point directly to the desired subsection. An example of how to do this for Alcohol septal ablation is provided in the documentation. What should I do if I misspell the name of a page I create? If a spelling error occurs in the title of a page, such as ST Elevation Myocardial Infarction, regular users are unable to move the page along with its history to a corrected title. However, it is possible to create a redirect. First, a new page with the correct title must be created, and the content from the old page must be manually copied to the new one. Then, the old page with the incorrect title should be edited, and its source code replaced with a redirect command pointing to the new page. What are undesirable redirects? Avoid creating redirects that point to another redirect. This is known as a double redirect. Double redirects do not function properly and can result in a slow and frustrating experience for the reader.
